Bumps the pip group with 1 update in the / directory: [anyio](https://github.com/agronholm/anyio). Updates `anyio` from 4.14.1 to 4.14.2
Release notes

Sourced from anyio's releases.

4.14.2

  • Changed ByteReceiveStream.receive() implementations to raise a ValueError when max_bytes is not a positive integer (#1191)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter.total_tokens rejecting float("inf") when the limiter was instantiated outside of an event loop. The adapter setter checked for infinity by identity (value is math.inf), so only the exact math.inf singleton was accepted, while every backend setter (using math.isinf()) accepts any positive infinity (#1189; PR by @​greymoth-jp).
  • Fixed to_process.run_sync() deadlocking when the worker function writes enough data to sys.stderr to fill the (undrained) pipe buffer. The worker process now redirects sys.stderr to os.devnull as well, matching the documented behavior
  • Fixed TLSStream.wrap() matching an internationalized (unicode) host name against the peer certificate using IDNA 2003 (via the standard library) instead of IDNA 2008, which could cause the host name to be matched against the wrong certificate (#1208)
  • Fixed anyio.open_process() (and run_process()) ignoring the extra_groups argument, as it mistakenly passed the value of the group argument instead (#1209)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter.acquire_nowait() and CapacityLimiter.acquire_nowait_on_behalf_of() raising trio.WouldBlock instead of anyio.WouldBlock on the trio backend when there are no tokens available (#1218)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter on the asyncio backend over-granting tokens (borrowed_tokens exceeding total_tokens and available_tokens going negative) when a non-blocking acquire was made in the window between a token being released and the notified waiter resuming. The freed token is now reserved for the woken waiter right away, so the non-blocking acquire correctly raises WouldBlock (#1170; PR by @​gaoflow)

title: GH#32368: prevent interrupted recovery archive growth
body:
## Problem

Resolves #32368.

The archive-first cleanup producer copies entire worktrees before pruning regenerable caches. A bounded cleanup timeout can interrupt this copy before metadata or `archive-complete` is written. Subsequent attempts create new timestamped buckets for the same source, so a cleanup intended to relieve disk pressure instead multiplies partial dependency trees. An observed installation accumulated tens of GiB this way. A separate ownership repair exposed this producer failure; permission diagnostics alone do not resolve it.

## Implementation

- `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_archive_copy.py`: exclude only proven ignored, untracked, allowlisted cache directories before copy IO, including nested cache roots beneath broader ignored directories. Preserve symlinks, tracked paths, and unknown ignored data. Stop on unavailable Git evidence.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-cache-policy.py`: expose copy, reservation, and completed-snapshot comparison through the existing fail-closed mode dispatcher.
- `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`: reserve one attempt per physical source identity under the existing producer lock before copying. Interrupted attempts cannot create additional buckets. Reuse completed snapshots only after existing Git identity validation and a current user-content/staged-state comparison.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-removal-audit-lib.sh`: regression coverage for pre-copy cache filtering, tracked/unknown data preservation, bounded repeated attempts, safe completed reuse, and refusal after new user data appears.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh`: copy the new archive module into the existing isolated profile fixture so its recoverable-cleanup path exercises the complete dependency set.
- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`: document interruption and operator-recovery semantics.

## Safety and scope

Existing source-removal guards remain unchanged. Unknown legacy partial archives are not automatically deleted or adopted. New incomplete attempts retain their reservation and require operator review; this intentionally pauses an unsafe retry rather than erasing possibly unique data. The original source remains intact on failure. This change bounds retries for an unchanged physical source; it is not authority to delete arbitrary home-directory data or bypass active-worktree protections.

The existing archive finalization still copies Git administrative state and rewrites the archived `.git` pointer before publication. Completed-reuse comparison therefore uses archive-local staged state, not the original live index.

title: GH#32498: OpenCode V2 parity: load framework AGENTS.md, sanitize service env, leave Tabby recovery dirs
body:
## Summary

OpenCode V2 (`opencode2`) was not loading everything OpenCode V1 loads, and its greeting could go missing. This PR fixes three parity gaps found while testing GH#32444:

1. **Framework guide missing in V2.** V1 loads `~/.aidevops/agents/AGENTS.md` (~6K tokens) through the `instructions` entry in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. The isolated V2 config had only `plugins`, so V2 sessions answered faster but without the framework guide. A canary probe showed V2 loads `<config>/opencode/AGENTS.md`, so setup now links the guide there.
2. **Service inherited a session/headless environment.** The live V2 service (`serve --service`, ppid 1) had inherited an OpenCode V1 session's environment: `OPENCODE_PID`, `OPENCODE=1`, `AGENT=1`, `AIDEVOPS_OPERATION_ID`, `AIDEVOPS_TABBY_SESSION_RECOVERY`, `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_ISOLATED_DB`, and a pinned `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR`. A headless flag inherited the same way makes `shouldInjectGreeting` return false for every session. One user session (`ses_f1f2d1520ffe…`) got 5 redistributed blocks instead of the usual 6, meaning no greeting block. The managed shim now drops that inherited state for service and TUI launches.
3. **Tabby recovery marker cwd.** Launching `opencode2` from a Tabby recovery marker directory left V2 in the marker dir. The shim now resolves the marker's project with `session-recovery-marker.mjs` and `cd`s there (falling back to `$HOME`). It never resumes the V1 session.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh`: `_setup_opencode_v2_link_framework_guide` symlinks the guide into the V2 config, called from the V2 branch of `setup_opencode_plugins`. It keeps user-authored files and symlinks pointing outside `~/.aidevops/`, and repairs stale managed links.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh`:
  - `# aidevops:opencode-v2-shim-version=2` marker, so existing shims regenerate;
  - `_setup_append_opencode_v2_session_guard` parses args (`--standalone`/`--server` keep the env; value flags are skipped) and unsets inherited OpenCode/aidevops session, worker, headless, Tabby, overlay and bundle-pin variables;
  - kept on purpose: `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`AIDEVOPS_OPENAI_API_KEY_SOURCE` for the OAuth pool, and `GITHUB_ACTIONS`;
  - Tabby marker-dir redirect for TUI launches.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/root-session-greeting-gate.mjs` (new): the V2 root-session greeting gate, moved out of `v2.mjs`. It skips child sessions silently and logs any other skip (headless env, no session lookup, lookup failure) once per session to `opencode-plugin.log`. A separate module keeps `ttsr.mjs` under the qlty complexity threshold.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`: wires the gate and logs when `AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_SESSION_GREETING` disables the greeting.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh`: comment only. The deploy-time restart already goes through the managed shim, which now sanitizes the env.
- Docs: `.agents/tools/opencode/opencode.md` (V1/V2 parity paragraph), `.agents/reference/context-efficiency.md` (greeting wording).

No double greeting: `~/.aidevops/agents/AGENTS.md` has no greeting text. The V1 greeting fallback lives only in `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md`.

Anthropic OAuth wire shaping (billing header plus identity in `system`, redistributed framework text, cch signing) and the OpenAI OAuth-pool path are unchanged.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-v2-setup.sh` → `OpenCode V2 setup tests passed`. New cases: link created, stale managed link repaired, user file kept, user symlink kept, shim version marker present.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-install-opencode.sh` → `84 passed, 0 failed`. New cases: inherited env dropped, `--standalone` keeps env, marker-dir cd, `$HOME` fallback, non-marker cwd kept.

- Full plugin suite in the mirror: 986/992. The 6 failures are in the signature-footer and source-access tests and come only from the isolated HOME; rerun with the real HOME they pass 111/111. None of those files are touched here.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the changed scripts and on a generated shim. `qlty smells` reports nothing on the changed files.
- The real marker resolver maps the user's Tabby marker to its original project checkout.

## Post-merge checks

After release and `aidevops update`:
- `~/.local/bin/opencode2` contains the version-2 marker;
- `<v2 config>/opencode/AGENTS.md` links to the framework guide;
- the restarted service env has no `OPENCODE_PID`/`AIDEVOPS_*` session vars;
- a fresh V2 session shows `core/instructions` in `instruction_state` and greets once.

This corrects the macOS MagicDNS troubleshooting step in `services/networking/nostr-vpn.md`. `sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder` does **not** make macOS re-read `/etc/resolver`. The fix that worked was a network change: cycling the default interface.

## Evidence (MacBook, macOS arm64, from #23846)

- After mDNSResponder HUP, `scutil --dns` still listed the **deleted** `fips` resolver and no `nvpn`, and `ping mini.nvpn` failed with `cannot resolve`.
- After `networksetup -setairportpower en0 off/on`, `scutil --dns` listed only `domain : nvpn`. `ping mini.nvpn` got 3/3 replies, and `ssh claudia@mini.nvpn hostname` returned `Mac` with the known fingerprint.
